answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to continuously cultivate a private computational garden of sequential zero-knowledge proofs generated with a unique quill signature chain. An attacker spawning N fakes must expend N times the serial CPU-seconds (roughly 45 seconds of dedicated core time per identity per epoch) to keep every garden fresh in the shared meadow of attested state; honest single agents pay only once and can reuse the same quill chain. Failure mode: if proofs are parallelizable without serial dependency, cost collapses.
